library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kozielska_2012_risperidone_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kozielska_2012_risperidone_rat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-012-0722-8> (open access, PMC3369128)

The model extends the hybrid physiology-based olanzapine model of Johnson 2011
(packaged as `Johnson_2011_olanzapine_rat`) to risperidone (RIS) and its active
metabolite paliperidone (PALI). Three additions distinguish it: metabolite
formation (including first-pass conversion after an intraperitoneal dose),
linear active efflux at the blood-brain barrier, and a second receptor pool
(5-HT2A in frontal cortex) beside the striatal D2 receptors. Both drugs compete
for both receptors with shared binding constants, and the measured occupancy is
the sum of the occupancy by the two drugs.

# Population

Data came from twelve single-dose studies in male Sprague-Dawley or Wistar
rats contributed by Janssen, Merck Sharp and Dohme, and Pfizer (Table I; 282
rats summed over the study rows). Risperidone was given IV, IP or SC at
0.01-40 mg/kg; paliperidone was given SC at 0.16-10 mg/kg in two studies.
Mostly one animal contributed one time point, because brain sampling is
terminal. Observations were plasma RIS and PALI; total brain,
brain-minus-striatum, brain-minus-frontal-cortex, striatum and cortex
concentrations; D2 occupancy in striatum ([3H]raclopride) and 5-HT2A occupancy
in frontal cortex ([3H]M100907), measured in vivo or ex vivo. No body weights
were available, so all parameters are per kg.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kozielska_2012_risperidone_rat")()$population`.

# Using the model

An IP risperidone dose is split between the risperidone and the paliperidone
central compartments, so it is entered as two dose records of the same amount
with `ROUTE_IP = 1`, one into `central` and one into `central_9oh`. An IV dose
goes to `central` with `ROUTE_IP = 0`. SC doses go to `depot` (risperidone) or
`depot_9oh` (paliperidone) with `rate = -2`, which makes the model's zero-order
duration apply before the first-order absorption.

The model declares six endpoints (`Cc`, `Cc_9oh`, `Cbrain`, `Cbrain_9oh`,
`D2RO`, `RO_5HT2A`), so observation rows carry `dvid = 1` and every endpoint
column is returned at every observation time. The other brain matrices the
paper measured are returned as output columns: `Cbrain_exstr` (brain without
striatum, the D2 studies), `Cbrain_excor` (brain without frontal cortex, the
5-HT2A studies), `Cstriatum`, `Ccortex`, `Cstriatum_9oh` and `Ccortex_9oh`.
Concentrations are in mg/L (multiply by 1000 for the ng/mL of the paper's
figures); occupancies are fractions.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Kozielska_2012_risperidone_rat")

# One rat (or one cohort of n rats) given a single risperidone dose by the
# named route, observed at `times`.
make_events <- function(dose, route, times, n = 1L, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_cmt <- switch(route,
    IP = c("central", "central_9oh"),
    IV = "central",
    SC = "depot"
  )
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, cmt = dose_cmt, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  doses$time <- 0
  doses$amt <- dose
  doses$evid <- 1L
  doses$rate <- if (route == "SC") -2 else 0
  doses$dvid <- NA_integer_
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = times)
  obs$cmt <- "central"
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$rate <- 0
  obs$dvid <- 1L
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs)
  ev$ROUTE_IP <- as.integer(route == "IP")
  ev$dose <- dose
  ev$route <- route
  dplyr::arrange(ev, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

solve_typical <- function(m, ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev,
    omega = NA, sigma = NA, keep = c("dose", "route"),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}
```

# Predictive check (Figure 4)

Figure 4 of the paper is a predictive check after IP risperidone: panels a-c at
1 mg/kg (plasma, brain without striatum, D2 occupancy) and d-f at 0.1 mg/kg
(plasma, brain without frontal cortex, 5-HT2A occupancy). The simulation below
draws 200 rats per dose with the model's between-animal variability and adds
the residual error of each endpoint (log-scale for concentrations, additive for
occupancy; the brain residual SD applies to every brain matrix).

```{r fig4-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20120322)
set.seed(20120322)
times_fig4 <- c(0.1, seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25))
ev_fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1, "IP", times_fig4, n = 200, id_offset = 0L),
  make_events(0.1, "IP", times_fig4, n = 200, id_offset = 200L)
)
sim_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_fig4,
  keep = c("dose", "route"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
n_obs <- nrow(sim_fig4)
sim_fig4 <- sim_fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    plasma = 1000 * Cc * exp(rnorm(n_obs, 0, th[["expSd"]])),
    brain = 1000 * ifelse(dose == 1, Cbrain_exstr, Cbrain_excor) *
      exp(rnorm(n_obs, 0, th[["expSd_Cbrain"]])),
    RO = 100 * ifelse(dose == 1,
      D2RO + rnorm(n_obs, 0, th[["addSd_D2RO"]]),
      RO_5HT2A + rnorm(n_obs, 0, th[["addSd_RO_5HT2A"]])
    )
  )

fig4 <- sim_fig4 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(plasma, brain, RO), names_to = "output") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel = dplyr::case_when(
      dose == 1 & output == "plasma" ~ "a: plasma RIS (ng/mL), 1 mg/kg",
      dose == 1 & output == "brain" ~ "b: brain RIS without striatum (ng/mL), 1 mg/kg",
      dose == 1 & output == "RO" ~ "c: D2 occupancy (%), 1 mg/kg",
      output == "plasma" ~ "d: plasma RIS (ng/mL), 0.1 mg/kg",
      output == "brain" ~ "e: brain RIS without cortex (ng/mL), 0.1 mg/kg",
      TRUE ~ "f: 5-HT2A occupancy (%), 0.1 mg/kg"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), q50 = median(value), q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fig4, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Kozielska 2012: median and 90% prediction interval, 200 rats per dose."
  )
```

The simulated medians follow the grey simulated-median lines of Figure 4:
plasma risperidone near 150 ng/mL at 0.25 h after 1 mg/kg and near 14 ng/mL
after 0.1 mg/kg, brain-without-striatum risperidone near 40 ng/mL at 0.25 h,
D2 occupancy about 75-90% over 0.25-2 h after 1 mg/kg, and 5-HT2A occupancy
rising from about 35% at 0.25 h to a peak near 1 h after 0.1 mg/kg. The 5-HT2A
median at 1 h (about 55%) sits somewhat above the Figure 4f line (about 48%);
the paper notes that its own model under-predicts the later 5-HT2A data. The
prediction intervals are wide, as in the paper, because the residual errors
are large.

```{r fig4-check}
med_at <- function(p, t) fig4$q50[fig4$panel == p & abs(fig4$time - t) < 1e-8]
fig4_check <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Plasma RIS at 0.25 h, 1 mg/kg (ng/mL)",
    "Brain RIS without striatum at 0.25 h, 1 mg/kg (ng/mL)",
    "D2 occupancy at 1 h, 1 mg/kg (%)",
    "Plasma RIS at 0.25 h, 0.1 mg/kg (ng/mL)",
    "5-HT2A occupancy at 1 h, 0.1 mg/kg (%)"
  ),
  figure_4 = c(150, 40, 87, 14, 48),
  simulated = c(
    med_at("a: plasma RIS (ng/mL), 1 mg/kg", 0.25),
    med_at("b: brain RIS without striatum (ng/mL), 1 mg/kg", 0.25),
    med_at("c: D2 occupancy (%), 1 mg/kg", 1),
    med_at("d: plasma RIS (ng/mL), 0.1 mg/kg", 0.25),
    med_at("f: 5-HT2A occupancy (%), 0.1 mg/kg", 1)
  )
)
fig4_check$pct_diff <- 100 * (fig4_check$simulated / fig4_check$figure_4 - 1)
knitr::kable(fig4_check, digits = 1,
  caption = "Simulated medians against the simulated-median lines read from Figure 4.")
# The Figure 4 values are read by eye from the grey median lines. The bound
# covers that reading error and the Monte-Carlo error of a 200-rat median
# (the medians of independent cohorts differ by a few percent); a wrong
# volume, clearance, Bmax or unit conversion moves these by a factor.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_check$pct_diff) < 35))
```

# Brain-to-plasma ratios (Figure 6)

The paper's central finding is that the risperidone brain-to-plasma ratio is
high at low plasma concentrations and levels off at about 0.25 as the
concentration rises, and that only the model with 5-HT2A binding reproduces
this. The ratio is computed below from typical-value predictions for the
doses, routes and sampling times of Table I.

```{r fig6-design}
design <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  # Total brain (studies 3b and 4)
  expand.grid(dose = 5, route = "SC", time = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8), matrix = "a: total brain"),
  expand.grid(dose = c(0.3, 3), route = "IP", time = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 7), matrix = "a: total brain"),
  # Brain without striatum (D2 studies 5-7)
  expand.grid(dose = 1, route = "IP", time = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), matrix = "b: brain without striatum"),
  expand.grid(dose = c(0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3), route = "IP", time = 1, matrix = "b: brain without striatum"),
  expand.grid(dose = c(0.16, 10), route = "SC", time = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24), matrix = "b: brain without striatum"),
  # Brain without frontal cortex (5-HT2A studies 9-10)
  expand.grid(dose = c(0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1), route = "IP", time = 1, matrix = "c: brain without cortex"),
  expand.grid(dose = 0.1, route = "IP", time = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), matrix = "c: brain without cortex")
)
design$route <- as.character(design$route)
design <- dplyr::distinct(design)
regimens <- dplyr::distinct(design, dose, route)

ratio_sim <- function(m) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
    make_events(regimens$dose[i], regimens$route[i],
      times = sort(unique(design$time)), id_offset = i - 1L
    )
  }))
  solve_typical(m, ev) |>
    dplyr::select(dose, route, time, Cc, Cbrain, Cbrain_exstr, Cbrain_excor) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(design, by = c("dose", "route", "time")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      brain = dplyr::case_when(
        matrix == "a: total brain" ~ Cbrain,
        matrix == "b: brain without striatum" ~ Cbrain_exstr,
        TRUE ~ Cbrain_excor
      ),
      plasma_ngml = 1000 * Cc,
      ratio = brain / Cc
    ) |>
    # Figure 6 shows only points with plasma above about 0.5 ng/mL.
    dplyr::filter(plasma_ngml > 0.5)
}

r_final <- ratio_sim(mod)
```

```{r fig6-abc}
ggplot(r_final, aes(plasma_ngml, ratio)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Plasma risperidone (ng/mL)", y = "Brain-to-plasma ratio",
    caption = "Replicates the final-model (grey) points of Figure 6a-c of Kozielska 2012."
  )
```

The paper's sensitivity simulations (Figure 6d-f) are reproduced on the total
brain: no active efflux (both CLefflux set to zero), kon and koff of both
receptors ten times higher (Kd unchanged), and koff of both receptors ten
times higher (Kd ten times higher).

```{r fig6-def}
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_noefflux <- mod_ui |>
  rxode2::ini(lcl_efflux = log(1e-12), lcl_efflux_9oh = log(1e-12))
mod_fastbinding <- mod_ui |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lkoff_d2 = th[["lkoff_d2"]] + log(10),
    lkoff_5ht2a = th[["lkoff_5ht2a"]] + log(10)
  )
mod_highkd <- mod_ui |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lkoff_d2 = th[["lkoff_d2"]] + log(10),
    lkoff_5ht2a = th[["lkoff_5ht2a"]] + log(10),
    lkd_d2 = th[["lkd_d2"]] + log(10),
    lkd_5ht2a = th[["lkd_5ht2a"]] + log(10)
  )
# kon = koff / Kd: raising koff alone with Kd fixed raises kon tenfold
# (`mod_fastbinding`); raising both koff and Kd keeps kon and raises Kd
# tenfold (`mod_highkd`).
scen <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  r_final |> dplyr::mutate(model = "final"),
  ratio_sim(mod_noefflux) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "d: no efflux"),
  ratio_sim(mod_fastbinding) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "e: kon and koff x10"),
  ratio_sim(mod_highkd) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "f: koff x10")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(matrix == "a: total brain")

scen_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("d: no efflux", "e: kon and koff x10", "f: koff x10"), function(p) {
  dplyr::filter(scen, model %in% c("final", p)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = p, line = ifelse(model == "final", "final model", "scenario"))
}))
ggplot(scen_plot, aes(plasma_ngml, ratio, colour = line)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("final model" = "grey60", scenario = "black")) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Plasma risperidone (ng/mL)", y = "Total brain-to-plasma ratio", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6d-f of Kozielska 2012."
  )
```

The final model reproduces the shape of Figure 6a-c: ratios level off near
0.25 at high plasma concentrations in all three brain matrices and rise as the
concentration falls. For total brain the rise matches Figure 6a (about 1.2-2
at 1-4 ng/mL). For brain without striatum and brain without cortex the rise is
about half of the paper's: about 1.0-1.2 at 0.6-1 ng/mL, where the grey
final-model points of Figure 6b-c reach about 2.4-2.8. This is discussed under
Assumptions and deviations.

Removing efflux raises the high-concentration plateau about fivefold, to about
1.1-1.3, and keeps the shape (Figure 6d); faster binding with unchanged
affinity lowers the ratios only at the lowest concentrations (Figure 6e); and a
tenfold higher Kd flattens the curve (Figure 6f).

```{r fig6-check}
lo <- function(d) median(d$ratio[d$plasma_ngml < 3])
hi <- function(d) median(d$ratio[d$plasma_ngml > 50])
by_model <- split(scen, scen$model)
fig6_check <- data.frame(
  model = names(by_model),
  ratio_low_conc = vapply(by_model, lo, numeric(1)),
  ratio_high_conc = vapply(by_model, hi, numeric(1))
)
knitr::kable(fig6_check, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Median total brain-to-plasma ratio below 3 ng/mL and above 50 ng/mL plasma.")
stopifnot(
  # Figure 6a: high-concentration plateau about 0.25-0.3, low-concentration
  # ratios several-fold higher.
  fig6_check$ratio_high_conc[fig6_check$model == "final"] > 0.15,
  fig6_check$ratio_high_conc[fig6_check$model == "final"] < 0.4,
  fig6_check$ratio_low_conc[fig6_check$model == "final"] >
    3 * fig6_check$ratio_high_conc[fig6_check$model == "final"],
  # Figure 6d: no efflux raises the plateau above 1.
  fig6_check$ratio_high_conc[fig6_check$model == "d: no efflux"] > 1,
  # Figure 6f: a tenfold higher Kd removes most of the low-concentration rise.
  fig6_check$ratio_low_conc[fig6_check$model == "f: koff x10"] <
    0.5 * fig6_check$ratio_low_conc[fig6_check$model == "final"]
)
```

# Closed-form checks

At steady state with the receptors saturated, the unbound brain-to-plasma
partition coefficient is set by the BBB clearances alone,
`Kp,uu = CLbev / (CLbev + CLefflux)`. A long constant-rate infusion of
risperidone into plasma at a high concentration checks that the brain
equations carry the unbound fractions and the efflux term the way the Appendix
writes them. The same derived constants reproduce the Table III `kon` values
and the efflux-to-passive clearance ratios the paper reports from its
likelihood profiles (4.57-4.87 for risperidone, 21.1-22.2 for paliperidone).

```{r closed-form}
ev_inf <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 0, 72), amt = c(2000, 0, 0), rate = c(2000 / 72, 0, 0),
  evid = c(1L, 0L, 0L), cmt = "central", dvid = c(NA, 1L, 1L), ROUTE_IP = 0L
)
ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_inf,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
ss_end <- ss[ss$time == 72, ]
kpuu_sim <- th[["fu_brain"]] * ss_end$Cbev / (th[["fu_plasma"]] * ss_end$Cc)
kpuu_sim_9oh <- th[["fu_brain_9oh"]] * ss_end$Cbev_9oh / (th[["fu_plasma_9oh"]] * ss_end$Cc_9oh)
p <- exp(th)
kpuu <- p[["lcl_bev"]] / (p[["lcl_bev"]] + p[["lcl_efflux"]])
kpuu_9oh <- p[["lcl_bev"]] / (p[["lcl_bev"]] + p[["lcl_efflux_9oh"]])
cf <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Kp,uu risperidone", "Kp,uu paliperidone",
    "kon D2 (1/nM/h)", "kon 5-HT2A (1/nM/h)",
    "CLefflux-RIS / CLbev", "CLefflux-PALI / CLbev",
    "D2 occupancy at saturation", "5-HT2A occupancy at saturation"
  ),
  expected = c(
    kpuu, kpuu_9oh, 1.45, 2.40, 9.97 / 2.13, 47.0 / 2.13, 1, 1
  ),
  model = c(
    kpuu_sim, kpuu_sim_9oh,
    p[["lkoff_d2"]] / p[["lkd_d2"]], p[["lkoff_5ht2a"]] / p[["lkd_5ht2a"]],
    p[["lcl_efflux"]] / p[["lcl_bev"]], p[["lcl_efflux_9oh"]] / p[["lcl_bev"]],
    ss_end$D2RO, ss_end$RO_5HT2A
  )
)
knitr::kable(cf, digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  # Same parameters on both sides: the steady state reproduces the closed form
  # to the solver tolerance (measured ~1e-7).
  abs(kpuu_sim / kpuu - 1) < 1e-4,
  abs(kpuu_sim_9oh / kpuu_9oh - 1) < 1e-4,
  # Table III rounds kon to three significant figures.
  abs(cf$model[3] / 1.45 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(cf$model[4] / 2.40 - 1) < 0.005,
  # Likelihood-profile ranges quoted in Results, Model Evaluation.
  cf$model[5] > 4.57, cf$model[5] < 4.87,
  cf$model[6] > 21.1, cf$model[6] < 22.2,
  ss_end$D2RO > 0.99, ss_end$D2RO <= 1, ss_end$RO_5HT2A > 0.99, ss_end$RO_5HT2A <= 1
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The plasma AUCs follow in closed form from the
typical-value clearances: risperidone `AUC = F * Dose / (CLRIS + CLmet)`, and
paliperidone formed from it
`AUC = F * Dose * CLmet / (CLRIS + CLmet) / CLPALI` (plus, after an IP dose,
the first-pass fraction `FIP * FrFPM * Dose / CLPALI`). PKNCA is run on the
typical-value profiles of three risperidone regimens from Table I.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- c(0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48)
regs <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("IV 2.5 mg/kg", "SC 5 mg/kg", "IP 3 mg/kg"),
  dose = c(2.5, 5, 3), route = c("IV", "SC", "IP")
)
ev_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regs)), function(i) {
  make_events(regs$dose[i], regs$route[i], nca_times, id_offset = i - 1L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = regs$treatment[i])
}))
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, keep = "treatment",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
)

conc <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, risperidone = Cc, paliperidone = Cc_9oh) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(risperidone, paliperidone), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc")
stopifnot(all(conc$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(conc$Cc)))
conc$Cc <- pmax(conc$Cc, 0)

dose_df <- ev_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, cmt %in% c("central", "depot")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, amt)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id / analyte)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cmax"))

f_route <- c("IV 2.5 mg/kg" = 1, "SC 5 mg/kg" = p[["lfdepot"]], "IP 3 mg/kg" = p[["lfip"]])
cl_tot <- p[["lcl_nonmet"]] + p[["lcl_met"]]
fm <- p[["lcl_met"]] / cl_tot
reference <- regs |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f = f_route[treatment],
    f_ris = ifelse(route == "IP", f * (1 - p[["lfpm_9oh"]]), f),
    f_fpm = ifelse(route == "IP", f * p[["lfpm_9oh"]], 0),
    risperidone = f_ris * dose / cl_tot,
    paliperidone = (f_ris * dose * fm + f_fpm * dose) / p[["lcl_9oh"]]
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, risperidone, paliperidone) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(risperidone, paliperidone), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "aucinf.obs")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"),
  reference = reference,
  by = c("treatment", "analyte"),
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 2
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "PKNCA AUC0-inf against the closed-form typical-value AUC. * marks rows differing by more than 2%.")
cmp_num <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(reference, by = c("treatment", "analyte"))
# Trapezoidal AUC on an 18-point grid against the exact integral: the
# difference is the trapezoid and extrapolation error, well under 2%.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_num$PPORRES / cmp_num$aucinf.obs - 1) < 0.02))
```

```{r cmax-table}
nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cmax_ngml = 1000 * PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, analyte, Cmax_ngml) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, values_from = Cmax_ngml) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment,
    "Risperidone Cmax (ng/mL)" = risperidone,
    "Paliperidone Cmax (ng/mL)" = paliperidone
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value plasma Cmax by regimen.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Brain concentration.** The Appendix gives the ODEs but not how a measured
  brain concentration maps onto them. The model takes the brain homogenate
  concentration as the total amount in the sampled brain compartments
  (vascular, extravascular, striatum free and bound, cortex free and bound)
  divided by their total volume. Brain without striatum drops the two
  striatum compartments, and brain without frontal cortex drops the two cortex
  compartments. This reading reproduces the Figure 4 medians, the Figure 6a
  ratios, and the high-concentration plateau of about 0.25 in every brain
  matrix. It keeps the 5-HT2A-bound drug in the brain-without-striatum
  concentrations, which the Results require (raising koff for 5-HT2A alone
  flattens exactly those ratios). At the lowest plasma concentrations
  (below about 2 ng/mL) its brain-without-striatum and brain-without-cortex
  ratios are about half of the grey points in Figure 6b-c. Dividing by the
  vascular plus extravascular volume alone (treating the 0.00656 L/kg
  "total extra-vascular" volume as containing the striatum and cortex)
  roughly doubles the low-concentration ratios but lifts the plateau to
  0.4-0.6, against about 0.25 in the paper, so it fits worse overall. No
  parameter was adjusted to close the gap.
* **Cortex transfer clearance.** CLcor is not given; the paper states only
  that fast equilibration was assumed "as for striatum". It is fixed to the
  striatum value, 500 L/h/kg.
* **Molecular weights.** The bound-concentration formula needs molecular
  weights that the paper does not print: 410.49 g/mol for risperidone
  (C23H27FN4O2) and 426.49 g/mol for paliperidone (C23H27FN4O3). The
  Appendix's factor `1000 / MW` is written for amounts in ug; the packaged
  model keeps amounts in mg and uses `1e6 / MW`, which gives the same nM.
* **Metabolite mass.** As in the Appendix, the formation term
  `CLmet * C_RIS` moves risperidone mass into paliperidone without a
  molecular-weight correction (paliperidone is 4% heavier).
* **IP first-pass split.** Figure 1 states that a fraction of the absorbed IP
  dose reaches risperidone central and a fraction (FrFPM) paliperidone
  central. The model applies FIP to the whole dose and splits it as
  `FIP * (1 - FrFPM)` and `FIP * FrFPM`.
* **IIV scale.** Table II reports IIV as %CV without giving the conversion.
  The variances use `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`, the convention the same group
  states in the predecessor olanzapine paper (Johnson 2011). The brain PK-PD
  parameters have no IIV, as in the paper.
* **Residual error.** Plasma and brain concentrations were fitted
  log-transformed, so the tabulated "proportional" errors are log-scale SDs and
  are encoded with `lnorm()`. The occupancy errors are additive in percentage
  points in Table III and are divided by 100 because the model returns
  occupancy as a fraction. The paper applies one brain residual SD per drug to
  every brain matrix; rxode2 cannot share one error parameter between
  endpoints, so only total brain (`Cbrain`, `Cbrain_9oh`) carries an error
  model and the other matrices are output columns.
* **No paliperidone IV data.** The paper had no IV paliperidone data. A dose
  into `central_9oh` with `ROUTE_IP = 0` is treated as IV with F = 1, which the
  data did not inform.
* **In vivo and ex vivo occupancy** share binding constants, as in the final
  model.
